dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a steady 1-day, 2200 ppm dip that is flat-bottomed and measured to come from the target star itself, with a size of about 2.2 Earth radii around a small M dwarf. The star spins at the same period and varies strongly by spots, and the orbit is grazing, which explains why the long duration and large spot signal made the automated planet rank low. With the centroid on target and no secondary eclipse, a planet remains the best explanation, pending mass measurement.

Star is dense for Teff 3430 K so duration is longer (ratio 1.68) than the canonical value; the fit shows the extra duration is explained by a grazing transit, not a stellar companion.
